description: Sienna, formerly known as SIIP, is a modular open-source modelling framework from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR, the former National Renewable Energy Laboratory) for building, solving and analysing scheduling problems and dynamic simulations of power systems. It consists of Julia packages: Sienna Data (PowerSystems.jl) holds a rigorous data model for generators, lines, transformers, HVDC, storage, loads, services and time series of millions of devices; Sienna Ops (PowerSimulations.jl) simulates unit commitment, economic dispatch, automatic generation control and nonlinear optimal power flow for production cost modelling; and Sienna Dyn (PowerSimulationsDynamics.jl) simulates dynamic response to perturbations, with phasor and balanced electromagnetic transient models and small-signal stability. It is location independent and scales to large systems. Packages are on GitHub (PowerSystems.jl version 5.12.3) under the BSD 3-Clause licence, free of charge; the contact is Clayton Barrows. Caveats: PowerSystems.jl supports only a limited number of input file formats, users need Julia skills, and NLR states that extending Sienna to other infrastructure systems and interdependencies is future work. Simulation uses are network flow, production cost optimisation, capacity planning and stability studies for resilience. Related records: it compares with platform-powsybl and platform-gridpath.
interoperability: several power system file formats parsed by PowerSystems.jl
